config.description: Three top-level groups. The request wire format (OpenAI / Anthropic / MCP) is DETECTED per request from the body shape, so there is no field selecting it: the two chat formats overlap, and a hand-set value silently scanned the user's message and nothing else.

skyflow.description: What to call, how to authenticate to it, and what to detect.

vault_configuration.description: The three values shown on the vault's own page in the Skyflow admin UI, under the same names.

vault_url.description: The vault URL as the UI shows it, e.g. https://ebfc9bee4242.vault.skyflowapis.com. Taken whole rather than assembled from a cluster id, because the host also encodes the environment -- a sandbox vault lives on .skyflowapis.tech. A trailing slash and a missing scheme are tolerated.

vault_id.description: Skyflow vault that stores tokens and resolves re-identification.

credentials.description: `method` selects which record is read, with NO fallback between them: under sts a populated bearer_token is never touched.

method.description: sts exchanges the CALLER's IdP token for a short-lived Skyflow bearer (RFC 8693), so the gateway holds no Skyflow credential at all.

token_header.description: Header carrying the caller's IdP token.

expected_issuer.description: Checked locally before any network hop, so an unauthenticated request costs nothing.

service_account_json.description: The whole service-account JSON. Encrypted and referenceable -- use a vault reference, not a literal.

deidentify.description: What counts as sensitive, and how it is tokenized.

entities.description: Entity types to detect, validated against the types the vault has columns for -- a typo is refused at save time rather than silently matching nothing. Empty means ALL. IGNORED when configuration_source = config_id.

token_format.description: VAULT_TOKEN is reversible and deterministic, and is what re-identification requires.

configuration_source.description: Detect models these as a protobuf oneof (`configurationSource`), so they are mutually exclusive on the wire. This SELECTS one and never merges: under config_id the entity list, token_format, destination_table and both regex lists are ignored, because the saved configuration owns every detection decision.

config_id.description: Required when configuration_source = config_id. Enforced here rather than left to the API, because an id that does not resolve reports 'Field vault_id or configuration_id is missing in the request' -- an error naming the wrong problem.

destination_table.description: The vault table holding the entity columns. Every entity tokenized as VAULT_TOKEN needs a destination table.column; the column is derived (NAME -> table1.name_entity) because the Detect vault schema follows that rule for every column. Only the table name varies.

allow_regex.description: Sent as `skip`: suppresses false POSITIVES, leaving matches as plaintext.

restrict_regex.description: Sent as `restrict`: catches false NEGATIVES, turning matches into [RESTRICTED] whether or not a detector fired.

token_preamble.description: Prepended to the outbound system prompt. Not part of the Detect call, so it applies under either configuration_source.

text.description: Overrides the built-in text. Without a preamble the model editorialises about redaction instead of using the placeholders, which measurably degrades answers.

reidentify.description: Restoring real values on the response leg.

enabled.description: On by default: without it the CLIENT also receives vault tokens, which is a valid posture but a surprising default.

strategy.description: reidentify_text resolves through the vault, so it restores tokens minted on an earlier turn. mapping_only uses the request-scoped map and cannot.

tool_inputs.description: Tool arguments the model sends back. Default keeps tokens: an unknown tool is assumed to ship its arguments somewhere the gateway does not control.

tool_inputs_by_tool.description: Per-tool override, keyed by exact tool name or a `*`-suffixed prefix (exact beats prefix; longest prefix wins). Tools that run on the caller's OWN machine need plain_text -- an Edit call whose old_string is a vault token writes that token into the user's real file.

operations.description: Cost, failure posture and telemetry. Nothing here changes which data is protected.

limits.description: Fail-closed ceilings rather than hints: exceeding one refuses the request instead of partially processing it. Transport and concurrency settings (per-attempt timeout 15s, whole-request deadline 60s, 2 retries, waves of 8, a 16-connection keepalive pool) are fixed constants in the plugin rather than fields -- they were derived from measurement, and pinning the wave width and pool size together keeps a wave from ever exceeding the pool.

max_spans.description: Cap on text spans per request; over it the request is refused with 413 rather than partly de-identified. Agent traffic needs headroom -- a short message can carry ~30 resent tool definitions.

on_error.description: Both default to deny, because forwarding a body the gateway could not process is the one outcome this plugin exists to prevent.

dry_run.description: Detect and log, forward the body unchanged. For measuring what a route carries before enforcing on it.

detections.description: Entity COUNTS by type. Never values.
